title: Smooth open of curves with isolated complete intersection singularities
statement: On schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $\mathcal C(T)$ be the groupoid of flat proper finitely presented morphisms $X\to T$ of algebraic spaces whose geometric fibres have dimension at most one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Arrows in $\mathcal C(T)$ are $T$-isomorphisms and pullback is cartesian base change; arrows over $T'\to T$ are isomorphisms $X'\cong X\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Algebraic spaces are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Flatness and local finite presentation for their morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed: separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion, finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (the scheme conventions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). Assume $\mathcal C$ has been shown to be an algebraic stack (representable diagonal and a smooth surjective scheme atlas). There is an open substack $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal C$ smooth over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with this characterization: for every field $K$ and every proper $K$-scheme $C$ of dimension at most one, the classifying point of $C$ belongs to $\mathcal L$ if and only if $C$ is a local complete intersection over $K$ and $C\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is smooth except at finitely many points. Here local complete intersection means an affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated local-complete-intersection $K$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]; smoothness is [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For an open substack, its pullback along any scheme-valued object is an open subscheme of the base; smooth over Z means that its smooth scheme atlas has smooth composite to Spec Z. Empty and disconnected $C$ are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0DZX (lemma-big-smooth-part-curves), clauses (1) and (3), with the open substack lci+ in the statement. This is the full isolated-lci locus, not the nodal locus.

proof.text: Let $f:X\to B$ be any family classified by $\mathcal C$. Properness makes its underlying map closed, and flatness and finite presentation supply the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-space-lci-base-open]. Obtain the universal open $B_{\mathrm{lci}}\subseteq B$ on which all fibres are local complete intersections. Its formation commutes with arbitrary scheme base change. In particular its field-valued points are exactly the lci curves, in the affine-cover convention of the statement.

source.place: Tag 0DZX (lemma-big-smooth-part-curves), intersection construction; Tag 0DZV (lemma-lci-curves) and its use of Tag 06CE.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-space-smooth-locus] to $f$ and write $U_f\subseteq X$ for its smooth locus. Its complement $T=|X|\setminus|U_f|$ is closed. Apply [lem-sfb-space-closed-subset-finite-fibre-open] to this closed subset and the proper map $f$. This gives an open $B_+\subseteq B$ commuting with every scheme base change, characterized by finiteness of the nonsmooth set of each fibre. The identification with the fibre nonsmooth set specializes the arbitrary-base-change assertion of [lem-sfb-flat-space-smooth-locus] to Spec(kappa(b)) -> B; finiteness can be checked over the residue field or its algebraic closure by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subset-finite-fibre-open]. Thus this works over imperfect fields as well.

source.place: Tag 0DZX (lemma-big-smooth-part-curves), intersection construction; Tag 0DZW (lemma-isolated-sings-curves), proof via the closed nonsmooth locus and Tag 0A4Y.

proof.text: Set $B_{\mathrm{good}}=B_{\mathrm{lci}}\cap B_+$. Define $\mathcal L(B)$ as the full subgroupoid of $\mathcal C(B)$ consisting of families with $B_{\mathrm{good}}=B$. Both opens commute with pullback, so this condition is stable under pullback. It is local on an etale cover: the complement of $B_{\mathrm{good}}$ is empty when its inverse image in a surjective cover is empty. Hence descent for $\mathcal L$ is descent for $\mathcal C$ with this local condition. For an object $X/B$ of $\mathcal C$ and a map $A\to B$, its pullback belongs to $\mathcal L(A)$ exactly when $A\to B$ factors through $B_{\mathrm{good}}$. Because $\mathcal L$ is full, the groupoid fibre product $B\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal L$ has the same functor of points as this open subscheme (the chosen isomorphism to $X_A$ removes all automorphisms). This proves that $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal C$ is an open substack. This is the direct test-object argument, without invoking a theorem about quotient presentations.

source.place: Tag 0DZX (lemma-big-smooth-part-curves), displayed intersection; section-open, universal properties, expanded using the definitions of full substack and fibre product.

proof.text: Over $B=\operatorname{Spec}K$, the good open is the whole one-point base exactly when $C$ is a local complete intersection and its nonsmooth set is finite. The first condition is precisely the affine-cover condition in the item, and the second says precisely that $C\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is smooth except at finitely many points. This proves both directions of the requested field-point characterization. Empty curves satisfy both conditions vacuously, and none of the construction requires connectedness.

source.place: Tag 0DZX (lemma-big-smooth-part-curves), clause (3), by the two opens constructed in steps 1 and 2.

proof.text: Now take any field-valued object $X/K$ in $\mathcal L$. It is a proper algebraic space over $K$, and its dimension is at most one: cover it by an etale scheme atlas of affine schemes $U_i$, each of finite type over $K$ because $X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is of finite type; the base changes $(U_i)_{\bar K}$ form an etale scheme atlas of the geometric fibre $X_{\bar K}$, so $\dim(U_i)_{\bar K}\leq1$, and [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-preserved-field-extension] gives $\dim U_i=\dim(U_i)_{\bar K}\leq1$. Hence [lem-sfb-separated-space-dimension-one-scheme] represents it by a $K$-scheme; separatedness and finite type follow from properness. The same lemma, applied to each affine open $V\subseteq X$ with $V_{\bar K}$ open in $X_{\bar K}$, gives $\dim X\leq1$ for this scheme. By the good-open conditions it is lci and smooth except at finitely many points. The criterion [lem-sfb-curve-smooth-locus-deformation-test] supplies a coefficient ring $\Lambda$ with residue field $K$ (equal to $K$ in characteristic zero and a Cohen ring in positive characteristic). Apply [lem-sfb-isolated-lci-curve-unobstructed] to this separated finite-type curve and this Noetherian local coefficient ring: every Artinian $\Lambda$-deformation lifts across every surjection, so $\operatorname{Def}_{X,\Lambda}$ is unobstructed. The equivalence in [lem-sfb-curve-smooth-locus-deformation-test] now puts this classifying point in the smooth open $\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal C$.

source.place: Tag 0DZX (lemma-big-smooth-part-curves), proof of (1), combining Tag 0DZU with examples-defos.tex Tag 0DZQ.

proof.text: For any scheme-valued object $B\to\mathcal L$, pull back $\mathcal M$ to an open subscheme $B_{\mathcal M}\subseteq B$. Every residue-field point of $B$ lies in this open by step 5. Therefore $B_{\mathcal M}=B$, and $\mathcal L$ factors through $\mathcal M$. Since $\mathcal L$ is open in $\mathcal C$, it is open in $\mathcal M$ as well. Restricting a smooth scheme atlas of $\mathcal M$ to this open gives a smooth scheme atlas of $\mathcal L$ whose composite to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is the restriction of a smooth morphism. Smoothness is local on the source by its definition on charts, so this restriction is smooth. Thus $\mathcal L$ is smooth over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 0DZX (lemma-big-smooth-part-curves), conclusion (1), using the smooth open from step 5 and the atlas definition of smoothness.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0DZX (lemma-big-smooth-part-curves), proof via Tags 0DZV, 0DZW, 0DZU and examples-defos.tex Tag 0DZQ; direct test-object expansion of section-open.

I read the item, all five new nodes and the sources in full. Stacks sources read: moduli-curves.tex 0DZX (statement and proof), 0DZV, 0DZW, section-open, 0DZU with the Cohen-ring paragraph before it; examples-defos.tex 0DZQ, example-schemes, section-general; spaces-more-morphisms.tex 06CE, 06CA, 0A4Y; spaces-morphisms.tex 0DZI; stacks-geometry.tex lemma-characterize-smoothness; algebra.tex definition-cohen-ring. The item and its citer are not on the side-live drop list, and the item is still unsplit in side-live, so the delivery is not superseded. Route: steps 1-4 build the 0DZX intersection: B_lci from the new 06CE node (properness gives the closed-map hypothesis), and B_+ from the 0DZI/02V4 smooth-locus node and the 0A4Y closed-subset node. Step 3 is the open-substack argument of section-open, done on test objects; it is elementary. Step 4 checks both directions at field points. Step 5 gets smoothness from the 0ADD scheme node, the 0DZQ node and the 0DZU node, with the same coefficient ring Λ. Step 6 shows L lies in M and is smooth; it is elementary. New nodes, all true and not duplicates: (1) lem-sfb-space-lci-base-open: for flat lfp maps, lci = syntomic = lci fibres, invariant under field extension; lem-trf-syntomic-locus-base-change is only a scheme source locus. (2) lem-sfb-space-flat-smooth-locus: true via 01V9 on charts; it honestly notes that 0DZI alone gives only flat base change. (3) lem-sfb-space-closed-subset-finite-fibre-open: a finite closed subset of the fibre consists of closed points, so the map is quasi-finite there and 0A4Y applies to the reduced subspace; this needs no lfp or Noetherian hypothesis, and base change and field-extension invariance hold. (4) lem-sfb-isolated-lci-curve-unobstructed: hypotheses equal to 0DZQ; Noetherian local Λ is a special case of section-general. (5) lem-sfb-curve-smooth-locus-deformation-test: the full 0DZU criterion for every proper curve of dimension at most one, so not a clause of the item; Λ = k in characteristic 0 works because k is flat over Z and Spec k → Spec Λ is of finite type. No new node restates the item (no D1). Fault fixed (C1/E1): step 5 used dim X ≤ 1 for a field-valued object X/K, but the stack only bounds the dimension of the geometric fibre. That node is added to uses and proof_deps and declared in split_report.tool_uses as a generic tool from unit sk-thm-p1 (precedent: lem-pc-dim-base-change).
